title: Illinois's 1st Congressional District election, 2026
description: The 2026 election for Illinois's 1st Congressional District pits incumbent Democratic U.S. Representative Jonathan Jackson against Republican nominee Christian Maxwell. The district covers the South Side of Chicago and parts of Cook, Will, and Kankakee counties, including areas such as Bronzeville, Hyde Park, Morgan Park, New Lenox, and Homer Glen. Jackson, first elected in 2022 and re-elected in 2024 with 65.8% of the vote, faces a Republican challenger in a district that is considered safely Democratic by major political forecasters. Key issues include economic opportunity, public safety, education, and federal immigration enforcement.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of June 2026. The district is rated 'Solid D' by The Cook Political Report, 'Safe D' by Sabato's Crystal Ball, and 'Solid D' by Inside Elections.

candidates.name: Jonathan Jackson
candidates.summary: Jonathan Jackson is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Illinois's 1st Congressional District, first elected in 2022. Born in Chicago to civil rights leaders Rev. Jesse Jackson and Jacqueline Jackson, he has a B.S. in Business from North Carolina A&T State University and an MBA from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management. He serves on the House Agriculture Committee and the House Foreign Affairs Committee and previously worked as a national spokesman for the Rainbow PUSH Coalition, where he advocated for criminal justice reform and international human rights.

candidates.name: Christian Maxwell
candidates.summary: Christian Maxwell is the Republican nominee for Illinois's 1st Congressional District, having won the March 17, 2026, Republican primary with 64.5% of the vote. She is a conservative businesswoman, e-commerce growth marketing consultant, and mother of four from Chicago's South Side. Maxwell holds a bachelor's degree from the University of Illinois at Chicago and has no prior political experience, running on a platform focused on economic opportunity, education reform, public safety, and reducing the tax burden on working families.

forecast.rationale: No public district-specific polls exist (0 polls). However, the fundamentals are overwhelmingly clear: incumbent Jonathan Jackson won re-election in 2024 with 65.8% of the vote in a Chicago South Side district rated 'Solid D' by Cook, 'Safe D' by Sabato's Crystal Ball, and 'Solid D' by Inside Elections. Republican challenger Christian Maxwell is a first-time candidate with no prior political office. The district's Democratic lean, Jackson's incumbency and name recognition, and the consensus of major nonpartisan forecasters all point to a safe Democratic hold. The 28-point margin estimate is consistent with Jackson's 2024 performance (~66% of the two-party vote). Confidence is medium due to the absence of any 2026 cycle polling, which limits direct measurement of current voter sentiment.
